releases.title: Quarterly P.O. Computed Amounts
releases.summary: Quarterly P.O. computed amounts now match the service visits inside the Product coverage period.

items.description: Quarterly P.O. amounts now divide across four visits for a one-year Product coverage period when the end date is the exact anniversary; the coverage-end anniversary is treated as expiry rather than an extra visit, and the full P.O. amount remains unchanged.

releases.title: More Appearance Themes
releases.summary: Choose from three additional accent colors while keeping the same light, dark, or system mode.

items.description: Appearance settings now include Purple, Pink, and Teal accent themes. The selected accent follows your account across the app and signed-out screens, including dark mode and offline app-shell pages.

After saving a TSR, the next new Create TSR form now refreshes the server-assigned sequence number instead of leaving the provisional 01 visible. Final saves remain authoritative on the server; daily per-engineer sequencing and offline queue behavior are unchanged.

Generated Calibration Reports now appear as direct download links on schedule cards and in the schedule file list. Existing TSR previews, certificate locks, and report access permissions are unchanged.

releases.title: Calibration Certificate Print Copy and Conditional Report Tables
releases.summary: Calibration Reports now omit unselected focal-spot tables, and approved certificates include a controlled hard-copy print copy.

items.description: Final Calibration Reports now include only the selected Small/Large focal-spot tables. Approved schedules show the additional No_Signature certificate filename as locked for engineers; it is reserved for administrator printing and is never sent to clients.

New certificate approvals atomically create the acting approver's signed PDF and an original-template No_Signature hard-copy PDF retaining the printed Rodito Aretano certifier block. Authorized administrators can preview/download the print copy; it is immutable and excluded from client-email packages.

releases.title: Calibration Certificate Catalog Matching
releases.summary: Calibration Reports now use canonical equipment names and model matches for consistent certificates.

items.description: Engineers select one of six approved Equipment Names and receive live canonical Equipment Model suggestions from the offline catalog. New certificates use YYYY-MMDD-BSID, while Calibration Report documents retain the engineer-entered model and calibration dates remain YYYY/MM/DD. Save Final Report closes the report editor only after the DOCX is durably saved; fallback storage or an unavailable catalog keeps finalization open with an actionable retry message.

New certificate requests snapshot the canonical equipment name and model used for approval. Existing pending requests continue to render their complete stored mapped values and certificate number unchanged through approval; incomplete historical snapshots remain Pending without generating a signed artifact.

releases.title: Calibration Certificate Numbers and Signatures Refined
releases.summary: New certificates use the controlled number format and clearer approver presentation.

items.description: New Calibration Certificate samples and submissions now use YYYY-MM-DD-BSID while the printed calibration dates remain YYYY/MM/DD. Existing pending snapshots remain unchanged, and generated signatures are cleaned, cropped, resampled, and placed with visible underline clearance.

Approved certificates now show the acting approver's snapshotted title and one fixed Medical Systems Division line, with suffix deduplication; legacy pending certificate numbers remain consistent through approval filenames and PDFs.

releases.title: Calibration Certificate Review Opens Reliably
releases.summary: Certificate review and Approval Notifications now remain available for routed approvers.

items.description: Calibration Certificate Review now opens the shared guarded detail modal and embeds its PDF as a preview without forcing a download. Approval Notifications and Mark All Read also handle pending Travel Liquidation notifications without returning an Internal Server Error.

releases.title: Calibration Certificate Approval Workflow
releases.summary: Calibration Certificates now use machine-owned BSIDs and a revision-aware routed approval workflow.

items.description: Engineers manage BSIDs in Product Inventory, see the machine-sourced read-only BSID and YYYY/MM/DD-BSID certificate number in Calibration Report, and receive queued, pending, returned, approved, and retryable certificate status with signed-PDF access. Sample and approved certificates now use one consistent regular data size, the restored original approver typography, a transparent certifier area, and a larger signature.

Assigned approvers can review Calibration Certificates, return them with required remarks, or approve them with their saved signature, display name, and configured title; signed PDFs remain immutable TSR history. Generated certificates preserve the patterned background, use the original Humanist approver styling, and render a substantially larger transparent signature.

releases.title: Calibration Certificate Sample PDF
releases.summary: Create TSR can now generate an unattached sample Calibration Certificate PDF from the supplied certificate form.

items.description: Engineers can enter a BSID in the Calibration Report editor and download exactly one flattened sample Calibration Certificate PDF. The unchanged canonical form is packaged as JavaScript-safe embedded data so Brave cannot intercept a raw PDF response before the form is filled; the certificate number combines the calibration date and machine BSID, and report equipment, hospital/facility, calibration, and TSR values are mapped into the supplied form. The sample remains unattached and incomplete values are reported without changing the finalized Calibration Report DOCX. Missing or corrupt embedded data produces a clear reload message without a download.

releases.title: Optional Calibration Reports in Create TSR
releases.summary: Create TSR can now capture an optional Calibration Report using the supplied Word form, then generate a layout-safe DOCX with recoverable local storage and retry-safe delivery.

items.description: Engineers can optionally complete the supplied three-page US Letter Calibration Report inside Create TSR. DOCX generation preserves the original Word layout and fills only existing blanks/signature data; destination-specific exact-fit validation rejects values that would add pages, punctuation and international client names remain intact, and the report now separates unattached Sample DOCX download from Save Final Report attachment creation. Sample DOCX generation may proceed with incomplete fields and warns about what remains missing, while the same feedback is shown inside the open report modal. The generated signature cell contains the enlarged signature image without repeating the engineer's name. Page 3 supports independent Small/Large focal spots with editable persisted sizes and Clear Form preserves the ordinary TSR while removing only report data/files. Generated Page 3 output now centers every inserted Small/Large measurement value and keeps the performance criteria table clear of the fixed footer by reducing the unused spacer before it without changing the supplied template. Latest-revision client email selection admits only the recognized generated DOCX, local Blob cleanup remains recoverable across edits/removal, and duplicate-token DOCX validation preserves idempotent retries without changing ordinary PDF/image attachments.

releases.title: One-Time Single-Visit P.O. Entries
releases.summary: Service Contract P.O. Details now supports one-time Single visits for machines without contract expiry.

items.description: Eligible Products marked No Expiry Set - No Contract can be saved as one-time Single P.O. visits using their Product Start Date, without changing their contract status. Contract-backed Single schedules remain annual, with one-time and Annual labels and fiscal/custom allocation filtering preserved.

releases.title: Service Contract P.O. Details
releases.summary: P.O. Details now records service frequency, Product coverage dates, and fiscal-period allocations.

items.description: P.O. Details now supports Single, Semi Annual, and Quarterly service frequencies, loads matching Product coverage dates, warns before changing a machine to Under Contract, and shows scheduled amounts for fiscal quarters or custom date ranges. Historical Contract and Single Visit rows remain readable.

releases.title: Accounting Handoff CC by Branch
releases.summary: Accounting Handoff CC recipients can now be maintained separately for Manila and Cebu/Davao requesters.

items.description: Settings now keeps separate Accounting Handoff CC - Manila and Accounting Handoff CC - Cebu/Davao lists. Approved Travel Request, Reimbursement, standalone Cash Advance, Travel Liquidation, and Cash Advance Liquidation handoffs copy the list selected from the requester's Engineer-profile branch; existing Manila rows and workflow-specific primary Accounting recipients remain unchanged.

releases.title: Shared PDF Upload Conversion
releases.summary: Receipt PDF uploads now stay within the stored size limit when a readable conversion is possible, with clear guidance when a document must be split.

items.description: Receipt PDFs are checked for readability, compressed from the original source while preserving pages and orientation, and rejected with an instruction to split the document when no readable version can fit the 2MB stored limit.

releases.title: Approval Notifications Stay Available
releases.summary: Approval Center now ignores incomplete legacy notification metadata instead of returning a server error.

items.description: Approval Notifications and Mark All Read remain usable when a legacy notification is missing event metadata; valid Submitted approval notifications remain visible and actionable.

releases.title: Reversible LPR Availability
releases.summary: Local Purchase Requisitions can be paused through deployment configuration while existing requests finish safely and parent workflows keep their linked documents.

items.description: LPR now supports normal, drain, and hard-off operation: new requests can be refused without stranding in-flight approvals, linked Travel Request/Cash Advance/Reimbursement documents, or their PDF handoffs.

releases.title: 1.5-Day Leave Requests
releases.summary: Leave Request now supports two-weekday requests with one full day and one selected AM or PM half-day.

items.description: Employees can request 1.5 days across exactly two weekdays, choose whether the first or last weekday is partial, and see the same duration in Calendar, approvals, history, HR handoff, and the PDF form.

releases.title: P.O. Equipment Picker
releases.summary: P.O. Details now loads every equipment record registered to the selected client instead of stopping after the first ten.

items.description: The equipment picker now shows all equipment registered to the selected client; the scrollable result list no longer truncates the client at ten machines.

releases.title: Register Confirmation Contrast
releases.summary: The warning confirmation on the P.O. and Reimbursement registers is now clearly visible in light mode as well as dark.

items.description: The warning confirmation on the registers uses a deeper amber so its bar and icon stay clearly visible in light mode as well as dark.

releases.title: Reimbursement Register Fixes
releases.summary: Reimbursement and P.O. register confirmations stay visible without moving the page, while filtered tracker totals and Excel exports stay aligned with the rows on screen.

items.description: Reimbursement Tracker filters now drive the visible KPIs and Excel export, including exact engineer filtering, viewed-batch scope, dated filenames, and a literal TOTAL row for Accounting.
P.O. Details and Reimbursement Tracker now show accessible fixed-position confirmations without scrolling to the top or leaking alerts into printouts.

releases.title: Multi-machine Purchase Orders
releases.summary: A single P.O. can now cover several registered machines, while exports, Products safeguards, and Equipment analytics stay aligned.

items.description: P.O. Details now lets you select multiple machines for one P.O., review them as removable chips, and edit the set without creating duplicate machine links.
The P.O. register still exports one row per P.O.; when several machines are covered, their serials and names remain aligned in the Machine columns and filters match any covered machine.
Equipment analytics now distinguishes purchase orders from machine links and shows link totals, so coverage and top-machine counts remain meaningful when one P.O. covers several machines.
Analytics now opens from the system start date through today, so historical service and purchase-order activity is visible immediately; week and month presets remain available.
Reimbursement Tracker rows now stay in one shared current batch across engineers; start a new batch explicitly when the batch changes, with existing records normalized to BATCH-032.
The Reimbursement Tracker now shows current-batch rows and totals by default, resets the register when a new batch starts, and offers an explicit all-batches export for history.
The Reimbursement Tracker now lets users switch the on-page register between the active batch and previously stored batches without exporting.
Equipment selection now shows Under Contract when the Products record marks the machine as contract-backed, instead of incorrectly presenting its warranty end date.

releases.title: Machine-scoped Purchase Orders and Equipment Analytics
releases.summary: Purchase orders now identify the installed equipment they cover, with safer Products-side reference handling and machine coverage analytics.

items.description: P.O. records can now be assigned to client equipment, searched and sorted by machine, and exported with machine serial and name details.
Analytics now shows machine-linked purchase order coverage, top machines and models, and the client worklist for P.O.s still missing equipment.
Dark mode fixes: the equipment picker's highlighted row on P.O. Details, the P.O. cards on phones, and the Cancel button on every request recall dialog are readable again instead of appearing blank.

releases.title: TSR Reliability and Records Improvements
releases.summary: Create TSR became safer and easier to complete, while frequently used records pages gained better sorting.

items.description: Engineer signatures are now required before a TSR can be saved.
Client email suggestions are now collapsed to reduce confusion, and internal Shimadzu addresses are excluded from client suggestions.
A soft reminder now identifies important TSR details that are still blank before final saving.
Save and error notifications automatically scroll into view.
Starting a new TSR or opening a new session now clears stale form details.
Saved TSR drafts are now visible and can be reopened from a dedicated draft list.
The Actions Taken section now uses more of the available first-page space before continuing to another page.
Product columns can now be sorted, and the selected sort order is remembered.
Long Travel Request schedule cards now retain a readable and consistent width.

releases.title: TSR Preview, Draft, and Workflow Updates
releases.summary: Final TSR review became more dependable, with stronger drafts, better PDF handling, and cleaner operational records.

items.description: Multiline Remarks and Recommendations now continue correctly instead of being limited to one printed line.
The Department field is editable while Radiology remains the default value.
Medical Center columns can now be sorted for faster record lookup.
Personnel with approver-only access are no longer shown as field engineers on the Calendar.
Zero-amount schedule rows are excluded during final submission while remaining available in drafts.
Activity Logs now classify newer TSR, reimbursement, travel, cash advance, approval, and accounting events more clearly.
Engineers must now review the final TSR PDF before confirming Save TSR.
The final TSR preview was resized for a professional layout with a default 100 percent zoom.
Draft loading now filters out unrelated and empty ghost drafts while preserving legitimate engineer drafts.
Engineers may explicitly apply their saved Settings signature instead of drawing it for every TSR.

releases.title: TSR Email and Save Protection
releases.summary: Multiple TSR attachments are handled more reliably, and blank or incomplete TSR files are prevented.

items.description: Schedules with multiple generated or uploaded TSRs now include the complete attachment list when sending email.
Engineers can review which TSR files will be attached before sending an email.
Additional payload safeguards prevent completed TSR PDFs from being saved with blank engineer-entered details.
Missing equipment and serial information entered in Create TSR is now captured more reliably.

releases.title: Cleaner Reimbursement Reports
releases.summary: Reimbursement Excel files now keep system work context separate from user-entered remarks.

items.description: Generated Excel reports now use separate Work Details and Remarks columns.
Remarks remain blank by default instead of repeating the client, task, product, and equipment details.
Schedules and manual items without clients now use cleaner Work Details wording.

releases.title: Sharper TSR PDFs and Smarter Travel Requests
releases.summary: TSR output quality, Travel Request conflict handling, supporting documents, and system update communication received major improvements.

items.description: Newly generated TSR PDFs now use sharp vector text, lines, and form elements for clearer viewing and zooming.
Urgent or retroactive Travel Requests can proceed when an exact matching client schedule exists within the travel dates.
Non-client commitments and overlapping Travel Requests remain protected as real conflicts.
Travel Requests now support up to 10 optional PDF or image attachments, with files up to 35MB optimized to 2MB when possible.
Approvers can preview Travel Request supporting documents, and Accounting receives one compiled supporting-attachments PDF.
A new What's New page provides readable daily system updates with account-based unread badges and acknowledgements.
The What's New page now lets users acknowledge all of their unread updates at once.
The What's New sidebar label and unread badge now display clearly together on desktop and mobile.
What's New is now available from a compact bell button in the desktop and mobile headers instead of occupying a full sidebar row.

releases.title: Private Bucket Storage Cutover
releases.summary: Managed system uploads now use private Railway bucket storage with verified migration and protected access.

items.description: TSRs, schedule files, reimbursement receipts, Travel Request attachments, and liquidation receipts now use private bucket storage.
All migrated upload files passed size and SHA-256 verification before the production storage cutover.
Settings now displays private bucket usage, total capacity, remaining space, percentage, connection, verification, region, and active storage mode.
Travel Request details and attachments are now limited to the requester, listed participants, and the specifically assigned approver through their dedicated workflow.
Queued TSRs now recover automatically from temporary connection failures, avoid duplicate saves, and resume pending supporting-file uploads safely.

releases.title: Accounting Attachment Controls
releases.summary: Supporting documents and receipts are easier to manage safely across every accounting workflow.

items.description: Editable reimbursements, travel requests, and liquidations now provide clear individual Delete and Delete All controls for uploaded files.
Cash Advance requests now support optional PDF and image attachments that approvers can review and Accounting receives with the approved form.
Attachment deletion remains available for Draft, Rejected, or Returned records and is locked after submission or approval.
Repeated receipt uploads are now detected by file content, preventing duplicate copies after double-clicks or upload retries.
Travel Request drafts now retain the selected check instruction, BPI account number, health condition, and special notes when reopened.
Generated Travel Request forms now show USD beside every requested amount when International / USD is selected.
Adding a manual reimbursement item now preserves all amounts and remarks already entered in the worksheet.
Generated TSR forms now wrap long customer addresses and automatically expand the information row so the complete address remains visible.

releases.title: Personal Appearance Themes
releases.summary: The complete system now supports account-synced dark mode and selectable accent themes.

items.description: Light, Dark, and Use Device Setting modes are now available across desktop, mobile, and installed PWA screens.
Classic, Shimadzu Red, Clinical Green, and Corporate Blue accent themes can be selected under Settings > My Account.
Appearance preferences follow each account across devices and remain available during offline work.
Dark mode now uses consistent readable surfaces across Calendar, Activity Logs, workflow pages, forms, tables, and mobile screens.
Local Purchase Requisition is now available for item purchasing with drafts, approvals, PDF forms, and Procurement handoff.
A Cash Advance or Travel Request can now include one supporting LPR with its own items, documents, preview, and approval signature.
The LPR attachment area is now simpler: use one Attach LPR action beside the request attachments, without extra list panels or confusing parent terminology.
The Office Supplies reimbursement category is now labeled Office/Field Items for clearer use in the worksheet, approvals, and generated Excel reports.
Multi-day TSRs show complete schedule coverage, while single-day team TSRs list other assigned engineers beneath Serviced By without repeating the service date and time.

releases.title: TSR Schedule Coverage Reliability
releases.summary: Multi-day TSRs now present linked service dates in a compact, readable format.

items.description: Multi-day TSRs now show a compact service-date range in the existing Date of Service field, while additional assigned engineers remain listed beneath Serviced By.
Send TSR now includes supporting PDF and image files from linked schedules, with uploads up to 35MB optimized to 2MB and limited to 10 manual files per linked job.
Office/Field Items now generate a required LPR review during reimbursement submission, with reconciled purchase lines, signatures, approval preview, and Accounting package inclusion.
Calendar dark mode now keeps schedule types visually distinct, improves grid and card contrast, and applies accent themes only to controls and selections.

releases.title: Multi-Branch Stock Inventory
releases.summary: Superadmins can now manage accountable Manila stock movements using barcode scanning.

items.description: Stock Inventory now manages separate barcode balances for Manila/Main, Cebu, and Davao with scanner-ready IN and OUT transactions.
Every stock movement records the branch, responsible engineer, transaction administrator, resulting balance, and any one-time correction reversal.
Superadmins can assign branch-specific Stock Inventory access or a focused Inventory-only workspace from Approval Routing settings.
Leave Request now supports signed planned leave, emergency Sick Leave marked Form to Follow, protected Calendar status updates, manager approval, supporting attachments, and HR email handoff.
Approved Leave Request emails now use separate Manila and Cebu/Davao CC recipient groups based on the requesting employee's personnel branch.

releases.title: Clearer Schedule Billing Tags
releases.summary: Schedules with a purchase order can now record the applicable SC or SV classification.

items.description: With P.O. schedules can now optionally be classified as either SC or SV, with the selected billing tag shown clearly on Calendar cards.
Superadmins can now manage newly generated TSR PDF filenames from Settings using safe placeholders and live billing-scenario previews.
TSR client email subjects now use independently managed Standard, Warranty, FOC, P.O., SC, SV, and Installation templates, with a clear choice for mixed TSR packages.
Send TSR now supports account-remembered Additional CC recipients and a read-only preview of the exact outgoing recipients, subject, message, and attachments.
Products now show Under Contract whenever active contract coverage is selected, while retaining clear expired-contract and no-expiry classifications.

releases.title: Product Coverage in Schedule Planning
releases.summary: Warranty and contract status is now visible while selecting equipment for a schedule.

items.description: Add/Edit Schedule now shows each selected product's current warranty or contract status without requiring a separate visit to the Products page.

releases.title: TSR Archive Sorting
releases.summary: The TSR archive now leads with the reports you filed most recently.

items.description: The TSR archive now shows the most recently added reports first, so a report you just filed appears at the top instead of being ordered by service date.

releases.title: Leave and Approval Workflow Improvements
releases.summary: Half-day leave and clearer Approval Center wording make request review more accurate and dependable.

items.description: Leave Requests now support 0.5-day AM or PM periods for every leave type, with time-aware conflict checks, Calendar blocks, approvals, and HR form output.
Approval Center review dialogs now keep the correct request type, requester context, action wording, and history labels even when a request cannot be opened.
Editable reimbursements now let engineers remove incorrect schedule or manual rows, keep them excluded after reopening, and restore one or all removed rows before submission.
Travel and Cash Advance Liquidation row deletion now gives clearer confirmation, recalculates balances, and cleans up linked receipt files more safely.
Engineers can now reuse monthly or custom reimbursement ranges while previously claimed schedules remain excluded and each historical request opens as its own record.

releases.title: Sign-In, Navigation, and Dashboard Refresh
releases.summary: Signing out now genuinely ends your session, sign-in gained self-service password reset, and the sidebar, engineer dashboard, and What's New page were rebuilt to be easier to read.

items.description: Logging out now fully ends your session. Previously the sign-in page appeared but the next action could quietly restore the same account, which made switching users unreliable.

A Forgot password? link on the sign-in page now emails a self-service reset link that expires in 30 minutes and can only be used once. Accounts without an email address on file are still reset by an administrator.
The sign-in page was redesigned with a show-password button, a Caps Lock warning, an online/offline indicator, and protection against double submissions. It now follows your selected accent theme.

Usernames typed on a phone are no longer rejected because of automatic capitalisation or a trailing space, and deactivated accounts now receive a clear message instead of looking like a wrong password.

The sidebar is now grouped into Main, Operations, and Records with a clearer active state, an account footer, full keyboard and screen-reader support, and pending counts beside Approvals and My Requests.
The engineer dashboard now opens with a Needs you today panel covering overdue visits, today's visits, continuation jobs, and parts or P.O. waits, replacing the row of summary tiles.
Dashboard sections can be reordered or hidden, and your arrangement now follows your account to any device instead of staying on one browser.
What's New now supports search, category filtering, and paging through 10 releases at a time, so an earlier update can be found without scrolling the whole history.
Administrators can now write, schedule, and target What's New updates directly in the app, preview them exactly as an engineer or approver will see them, and revert an in-app edit.

Administrators can now email a What's New digest from the app, with a new What's New Announcements recipient group in Settings, a preview of the exact message before sending, and a send-to-myself test. Sending stays switched off until it is explicitly enabled.

The What's New digest can now be sent to everyone in a chosen audience, with the recipient count shown before sending and any account missing an email address listed by name. Administrators can also tick exactly which updates go into each send.

The scheduler dashboard is now a single priority queue instead of three overlapping lists. It opens with a dispatch status line, and each count above it — overdue, unassigned, waiting on P.O. or parts, pending TSR — filters the queue when selected. Selecting a row loads it straight into the assign and reschedule panel.

Engineer availability now reflects real workload, including overdue visits and blocked jobs, and selecting an engineer assigns them to the schedule chosen in the queue. The dashboard also loads faster for scheduler accounts, which were downloading the full company task list without displaying it.

The manager dashboard now opens with the requests waiting on you, broken down by type, with how long the oldest has been waiting and a warning when anything has sat for more than five days. Previously the dashboard showed no approval information at all.

A new Direction panel compares the last seven days with the seven before it for completed visits, scheduled visits and TSR completion. Current totals such as overdue and pending TSR are shown without a comparison, because a past figure for them cannot be reconstructed accurately.

Severe overdue visits, aged TSRs, blocked jobs, repeat equipment and at-risk clients are now one ranked list instead of four overlapping panels, with each item appearing once. The dashboard also loads faster, replacing four large queries with one.

For accounts that are both an administrator and an engineer, the dashboard's shortcuts are now a single block listing each destination once. Timeline, Clients, Products, Engineers, Reports and Activity Logs were previously repeated across three separate sections, with Clients appearing three times.
Personnel, medical centre and product totals now appear as a single line on the manager dashboard. They previously sat in a section that no account could actually see.

releases.title: Clearer Dashboards for Managers and Admins
releases.summary: The dashboard now separates your team's work from your own, the manager dashboard is no longer mixed with personal assignments for the manager account, and the developer preview switcher was removed.

items.description: If you hold both admin authority and an engineer profile, your dashboard now marks where your team's overview ends and your own assignments begin, under a Your own work heading. Your personal sections keep everything they showed before.

The two Waiting figures on the same dashboard are now labelled by scope: Waiting P.O / parts, company-wide for the operation, and waiting, yours for your own visits. They previously carried the same word for different numbers.
The manager account now sees the manager dashboard on its own, without personal engineer sections stacked underneath. Engineer tools, permissions and schedule assignment are unchanged.

The Recent System Activity panel was removed from the dashboard. It could not be displayed by any account, so its live refresh never ran. The full activity log is unchanged and still available from the Logs page.
The developer dashboard preview switcher was removed. Checking how a role sees the dashboard now means signing in as an account that holds that role.

releases.title: Reports Is Now TSR Files
releases.summary: The Reports page is renamed to TSR files everywhere it appears, and a redundant tag was removed from the reimbursement page.

items.description: The Reports page is now called TSR files, in the sidebar, on the page itself, and on the dashboard shortcut. Nothing about the page changed apart from its name.
The "Personal reimbursement only" tag was removed from the reimbursement page. It repeated what the page already makes clear.
Signatures on the generated LPR form now sit on their own lines. The approver signature was printing one row too high, over the Invoice No. field, and the requester signature over Equipment.

Engineers can now add a schedule with no signal. It is saved on your device, shown on the calendar as waiting to sync, and sent automatically when you are back online. Open the calendar once with a connection first so your client and product lists are stored for offline use.

A schedule added offline is checked against the copy saved on your device and warns you about a likely clash before it is queued. If it still conflicts when it reaches the server, it is held for you to fix rather than double-booking anyone.

releases.title: Write the TSR Before the Schedule Syncs
releases.summary: A schedule added with no signal can now have its TSR written on site straight away, instead of waiting for the schedule to reach the server first.

items.description: Create TSR now works on a schedule that is still waiting to sync. Tap Create TSR on the card exactly as you would for a saved schedule, and write the report on site while the details are fresh.

A TSR written this way is sent only after its schedule has reached the server and been given its place on the calendar, so the two always end up linked. Until then it shows as waiting for its schedule.
On a multi-day schedule the TSR is filed against the day you actually did the work, taken from the service date on the report rather than the first day of the range.
Schedules still waiting to sync now appear in the schedule picker on the Create TSR page, marked as waiting to sync, so you can find them from the sidebar as well as from the calendar card.
If the schedule a TSR was written for is removed from the queue, the TSR is kept rather than deleted with it. It asks you to pick a schedule instead, so work written in the field is never lost.
Fixed "Unable to assign the next TSR number", which could block saving a TSR entirely. If it ever appears again it now names the reason instead of stopping with a bare message.

Saved TSR drafts now stay attached to their schedule even when your schedule list changes. If a draft's schedule really is gone, everything you typed is kept and you are asked to pick the schedule again rather than the draft failing at save time.

Adding a schedule with no connection now explains itself when it cannot be saved on the device, instead of the Save button appearing to do nothing. Saving without a connection stays limited to new schedules on engineer accounts.

A TSR now queues when your phone shows a connection but the server cannot be reached. Previously only a fully offline phone queued, so saving in a weak signal area failed outright instead of holding the TSR for later.

After the app updates, adding a schedule with no signal keeps working. Previously an update followed by losing signal before opening the app once online could quietly disable offline schedule creation.

Fixed a saved TSR draft losing track of its schedule, which caused "Selected schedule was not found" when saving. If a schedule really has been deleted, the TSR now keeps your work and takes you straight to the schedule picker instead of stopping.

releases.title: Safer Offline TSR Storage
releases.summary: Offline TSR drafts and queued PDFs now use durable browser storage without duplicating large files in localStorage.

items.description: Queued TSR PDFs and supporting files are stored as local IndexedDB blobs, while the localStorage mirror keeps only lightweight metadata.
When a final TSR save cannot complete, the app now reports whether the draft was actually preserved and offers the generated PDF as a download escape hatch when needed.
Create TSR warns engineers before browser storage becomes critically full so pending work can be synchronized or downloaded in time.

releases.title: Branch-Scoped Stock Inventory Viewing
releases.summary: Engineers can now view branch stock accountability without changing inventory records.

items.description: Engineers can view items and movement history for their assigned branch, with current borrowed items shown first so accountability is easy to check.
Reimbursement downloads now use one saved total across the worksheet, Excel, PCV, Request for Payment form, and accounting package, with clear warnings when legacy data needs review.

releases.title: Stricter Stock Inventory Branch Assignment
releases.summary: Assigning a Stock Inventory branch to an account now requires a real branch code, so a mistyped value cannot quietly grant access to a branch.

items.description: The Stock Inventory branch on an account must now be a real branch code (BC01, BC02 or BC03). Typing a branch name such as "Cebu" is no longer accepted there and the account is denied access until a proper code is set. Engineer accounts are unaffected — their branch still comes from their engineer profile.

releases.title: HR Schedule Viewer
releases.summary: HR can now review deployment schedules in a focused, read-only calendar.

items.description: Superadmins can grant a focused HR Schedule View that shows client names, assigned engineers, dates, times, and status while keeping schedule changes, commercial details, contact information, and TSR files unavailable.

The HR schedule export now hides the same details the HR calendar hides. The downloaded CSV previously included the free-text job title and the equipment name even though the on-screen calendar replaced them, and the export is again limited to admins and dedicated HR accounts rather than any account carrying the HR flag.
Superadmins can now create Engineer, HR, or Approver accounts from Add Personnel; restricted permissions are validated at creation and non-engineer accounts are managed from Settings.

A refused permission combination now names the switch that actually conflicts instead of always naming Approver-only and Stock Inventory-only, and Initials are asked for only when creating an engineer, since HR and approver accounts have no personnel record to store them on.

Named superadmins can now record provisional leave from the Calendar while the employee completes the signed form; approval replaces the provisional block without creating duplicate leave entries. This is separate from the emergency Sick Leave Form to Follow flow.

When an approved Leave Request replaces a provisional one of a different type, the audit trail and the notice sent to whoever plotted it now name both leave types, so a Vacation Leave placeholder replaced by approved Sick Leave says so. Superseded requests are also counted separately from approved leave rather than going uncounted.

Requesters can now withdraw their own Submitted Leave Requests, Reimbursements, Travel Requests, Cash Advances, and LPRs with a required reason before approval. The request returns to an editable state, pending approval notices are cleared, and the recall is recorded in the audit trail.

Superadmins can now grant focused Personnel management, Reports, or Schedule management access from Settings without granting full system-management authority. Each capability remains separate from restricted Approver-only, HR Schedule, and Stock Inventory-only views.

The regional administrator's calendar scope is limited to Cebu and Davao again. While the new Schedule management capability was being added, the check that grants it was placed ahead of the regional administrator's branch rule and briefly allowed Manila schedules as well. Named superadmins and accounts granted the capability are unaffected.

Schedule details now show recognized TSR documents with direct in-app preview links. Mobile View Files stays inside the existing detail sheet, while unsupported or legacy attachments are identified without dead links.

releases.title: Client P.O. Details Register
releases.summary: Authorized users can now keep a clear, searchable record of client purchase orders.

items.description: The new P.O. Details register records a client, P.O. date, P.O. number, and whether the order is a Contract or Single Visit, without adding financial amounts.
Superadmins can grant P.O. records access from Settings. Authorized users see the P.O. Details link under Records and can add, edit, or delete entries.

CSV and Excel exports are now always generated by the server and are never stored on the device. Exports need a connection: on a shared device this stops one account's download being reused for another, and it keeps every file matched to what your own account is allowed to see.

When provisional Leave cannot be recorded, the Calendar now shows the actual reason instead of a generic message. Weekend-only ranges, invalid dates, and clashes with an existing schedule or Leave Request each say what to change.
Analytics now leads with period-over-period service trends, branch concentration, service mix, open client work, and engineer workload instead of disconnected Today, Week, and Month tiles.
Authorized reports and P.O. users can now see company-wide purchase-order counts by type, client, and month without exposing monetary values or personnel analytics to P.O.-only accounts.
Analytics charts now follow the active theme, provide screen-reader data tables, clear failed-refresh values, support print output, and remain usable on mobile.
Analytics panels now keep their own content height, so a short status summary no longer appears as a large empty block beside a longer workload table.
Purchase order reporting now appears on Analytics for anyone who can read reports, not only for accounts granted P.O. records access.

Only the schedule total is compared with the previous period. Active, open and completed counts now state that they are a status as of today, because recent work has had less time to finish and a comparison there would read as a change in performance when it is not. Branch and service-mix changes now sit in the chart itself instead of a second list below it.

releases.title: Analytics on Phones, and a Cleaner Sign-Out
releases.summary: Analytics charts now fit the screen they are read on, and signing out clears the pages this device had stored for your account.

items.description: Analytics charts are now drawn to the width of the screen instead of scrolling sideways on a phone. Long branch and category names are shortened to fit, with the full name still shown on tap and in the printed table.
The service volume trend now shows fewer date labels on narrow screens so they stay readable, and every bar still names its date and both periods when tapped.

Signing out now clears the pages and data this device had stored for your account, so the next person to sign in on the same device cannot open them offline. Schedules and TSRs waiting to sync are not affected and remain safely queued.
Saved requester and approver signatures are now stamped larger and more consistently across generated TSRs, travel requests, reimbursements, cash advances, liquidations, LPRs, and Excel forms.

Create TSR drafts now remain available through an account backup when the browser clears local site data; supporting file blobs stay on the original device and are clearly identified for re-selection.
Reopening a saved LPR now restores its draft identity, so adding items and saving again updates the same requisition instead of showing a different-draft error.
LPRs with more than eight items now keep the official form layout, repeated request details, and signatures on every continuation page.
System Backup now remains downloadable when an individual bucket file, storage connection, or slow bucket response has a temporary problem, with clear warnings recorded inside the ZIP manifest.

Downloading a System Backup no longer ends on the "you are offline" page while you are online. The download is now handled directly by the network, so any real problem is reported instead of being replaced by the offline screen.

System Backup now contains the data that cannot be recreated - database, uploads and bucket files - and no longer bundles a copy of the application code. In testing this cut the archive from 82 MB to 39 MB and roughly halved the time it takes to build.

releases.title: TSR Drafts Back Up for Everyone, and Bookmarks Remember Where You Were
releases.summary: Every account that can open Create TSR can now back a draft up to that account, and signing in returns you to the page you originally opened.

items.description: TSR drafts now back up to your account for every user who can open Create TSR. Previously only engineers and system administrators were backed up - other accounts could write a draft that stayed on that one device even though the panel said it had been saved to the account.

If a draft cannot be backed up, Create TSR now says whether it will retry, whether you need to sign in again, or whether this account cannot back drafts up at all - instead of always promising a retry.
Opening a bookmarked page while signed out now returns you to that page after you sign in, instead of always landing on the Dashboard.
Downloading a System Backup no longer freezes the app for everyone else while the archive is being built, and a slow backup is no longer cut off partway through.
When you are offline and a screen needs something this device has not saved, it now says you are offline instead of showing a half-loaded page with missing numbers.
The sidebar and top-bar controls - What's New, appearance, and the navigation toggle - are now full-size tap targets on phones instead of small icons that were easy to miss.

releases.title: LPR Pages Stay Together
releases.summary: Every LPR page now identifies its request, item range, and position in the complete requisition.

items.description: Generated LPR pages now carry the LPR number, item range, and a PAGE X OF Y marker so detached pages can be recognised as part of one requisition.

Superadmins can now build a consistent system backup in the Backup Center, review database and storage warnings, and download the finished archive with resumable support without replacing the live database.

releases.title: Regional Administrators Can Record Provisional Leave
releases.summary: Regional administrators can now record branch-scoped provisional Leave blocks while employees complete and submit the signed form.

items.description: Regional administrators can record provisional/Form-to-Follow Leave for Cebu and Davao personnel. Manila targets remain protected, and the employee still completes and submits the signed formal Leave Request.
P.O. Details now records Start and End Dates and optional PHP amounts, with a complete filtered Excel export for the register.

releases.title: Backup Center Behaves Offline
releases.summary: Opening Backup Center without a connection now shows the usual offline screen instead of a browser error page.

items.description: Opening Backup Center while offline now shows the app's own "You are offline" screen, and its status panel reports that you are offline, instead of the browser's error page.

releases.title: Reimbursement Tracker
releases.summary: A standalone register for reimbursement batches, with control numbers assigned automatically and a one-click Excel export for Accounting.

items.description: Authorized staff can now record standalone reimbursement batches, calculate control numbers from Personnel initials and batch references, and export the Accounting register to Excel.

releases.title: Reimbursement Tracker Fixes
releases.summary: The Add and Edit form now scrolls, and the batch number continues from where the tracking workbook left off.

items.description: The Add and Edit reimbursement form can now be scrolled, so the expense categories, paid fields, remarks, and the Save button are reachable on any screen size.
New rows are suggested starting at BATCH-032, continuing the tracking workbook's sequence instead of restarting at BATCH-001, and the reference is filled in for you rather than left blank.

Reimbursement Tracker exports now contain only the seven Accounting columns, paid rows can notify the engineer with configured CC copies, duplicate initials are guarded, and recent amounts can be chosen from per-engineer suggestion chips.

releases.title: P.O. Details Summary
releases.summary: Purchase Order summary cards now show the total amount for Contracts and Single Visits.

items.description: The Contracts and Single Visits summary cards now show their respective total amounts alongside the record counts.
